header: r17.L2 · The security engineer who has watched a host fall · opus
verdict: Met for the delta, with no Blocking or Required finding: four of five round-16 findings resolved as stated and one (R16-11, M) in part. The largest gap is Advisory and sits on this lens's own success line: once the first entry says narrowed, the state can be undone by routine events (a re-created sandbox taking a global secret, a replaced token, a host push that reloads the authentication key), no read is due at those events or after block O7, and a later not narrowed entry widens the blast radius back with no decision, owner or deadline, only a text restore.
prior_resolution_notes: L2-r16-1 (R16-04, A): resolved as stated. Read 2 has three parts (the forwarding setting, the socket's keys, the account's SSH keys page) and cites 06 6.4. A residual gap is new: the socket may hold keys other than the signing key (L2-r17-2).

L2-r16-2 (R16-06, A): resolved as stated. The two rows are named, a time is added to same-date headings, and a not narrowed entry is an event of the four rows. Leaving out the approval-line row of 05 5.4 is right, since that row states the narrowed token's abilities, not whether it holds. New gaps on the widening itself and the forward edit (L2-r17-3, L2-r17-4).

L2-r16-3 (R16-11, M): resolved in part. The cadence (O3, O6, O7) is in the note and the dedicated socket is a recommendation in O8, as the M status says. The pass's stated limit ('how the forwarding stops is the maintainer's choice; an entry whose read 2 finds an authentication key reopens it') is in round-16.md only; a grep of the note, the index, the spec pages, the plan and the ADRs finds it nowhere, and the note still lists two limits. The cadence misses the events that change the state and ends at O7 (L2-r17-1, L2-r17-5).
L2-r16-4 (R16-10, A): resolved as stated. The token narrowing row's after-state says deploy keys, webhooks and collaborators added before the narrowing are not read, citing the note's two limits.
L2-r16-5 (R16-05, A): resolved as stated. The first narrowed entry has a fourth part, item h runs only once a narrowed entry exists and saves there, and O8's pass names both.

findings.section: the note on the maintainer block (The token narrowing, the cadence of later reads); plan (block O8); 05 5.4 (the token row)
findings.defect: Later reads are tied to the sittings of O3, O6 and O7, not to the events that change the narrowed state, and none is due after O7. The events are a re-created or restarted development sandbox, a `sbx secret set` again, a fine-grained token replaced at expiry, and the maintainer's own host pushes inside a sitting. O8 says 'set it as the sandbox's github secret' without saying sandbox-scoped, nor what becomes of a global `github` secret that holds the operator's token. A replaced token also never re-runs item h.
findings.scenario: After v1.0.0 the development sandbox, which is disposable, is re-created. It takes the global `github` secret, the operator's broad token (inferred: a global secret applies to a re-created sandbox when no sandbox-scoped one is set). No read is due after O7, so the note's last entry still says narrowed, and the four rows fired on that premise stay fired. In a sitting of O6, if the forwarded socket is the host's own agent, a read made before the host pushes passes, and a push with AddKeysToAgent then puts the authentication key back (inferred).
findings.change: In the note, make each of these an event at which a read is due, in addition to the sittings: a re-creation or restart of the development sandbox, any `sbx secret set` of its `github` secret, a token replacement (which also re-runs item h into that entry), and, within O3 and O6, a read placed after the maintainer's host pushes. Make the cadence continue after O7, for example at each release-candidate tag. In O8, name the sandbox-scoped secret and say that no global `github` secret holds the operator's token, or that read 1 reads which secret the sandbox resolves. Then state the R16-11 limit in the note's limits paragraph with its reopener. Cost: three sentences in the note and one clause in O8. No ADR decision or accepted risk changes; ADR 0011 decision 2 decides that the forwarding stops, and these are reads of whether it holds.
findings.evidence: Read at 54f674c: docs/notes/maintainer-block-of-ci-bootstrap.md:122-124 'one for each later read, which is due at each sitting of blocks O3, O6 and O7'; docs/plan.md:221 (O8) 'set it as the sandbox's `github` secret, stop forwarding the GitHub authentication key'; docs/plan.md:219 (O6) 'each host pushing from its own clone through its hook'; docs/spec.md:238 (Q19) 'romeu sets `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` to `signing.agentSocket` for the sbx calls'; docs/reviews/round-16.md (Write pass, R16-11) 'Stated limit: how the forwarding stops is the maintainer's choice; an entry whose read 2 finds an authentication key reopens it' (found by grep in no spec page, note, plan or ADR). Inferred, not measured: that sbx forwards the caller's `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` (A12, B2 measure it), that a global secret reaches a re-created sandbox (from the sandbox's own instructions, outside the clone), and that AddKeysToAgent or a keychain reload re-adds a key.

findings.section: the note on the maintainer block (The token narrowing, read 2, expected answer); 06 6.4 (signing rule, I34)
findings.defect: Read 2 expects 'the signing key and no GitHub authentication key', and the account page check covers only the signing key's fingerprint. 06 6.4's rule is that the socket holds exactly one key. A socket that holds the signing key plus another key passes when that key is a deploy key of another repository or a key of another GitHub account, since neither is on the operator's SSH keys page.
findings.scenario: The maintainer forwards a socket with the signing key and a work key that is a write deploy key on another repository (inferred: deploy keys are listed per repository, not on the account's SSH keys page). Read 2's three parts match, the entry says narrowed, and git over SSH from the sandbox still writes outside this repository.
findings.change: Expected: the socket holds exactly one key, the signing key, as 06 6.4 states. If that reads as deciding how the forwarding stops, which ADR 0011 decision 2 leaves open, the alternative is that the entry lists every key of the socket by fingerprint with what it opens, and any key not shown to open nothing makes the verdict not narrowed. Cost: one clause in read 2. No ADR decision changes.
findings.evidence: Read at 54f674c: docs/notes/maintainer-block-of-ci-bootstrap.md:158-159 'Expected: the setting names one socket; that socket holds the signing key and no GitHub authentication key'; docs/spec/06-kits.md:100-101 '`signing.agentSocket` is set, reachable, and holds exactly one key, and that key equals the kit's `signingKey` arg'. Inferred, not read from GitHub's documentation this round: where deploy keys are listed.

findings.section: the note on the maintainer block (The token narrowing, the return rule); 05 5.4 (the token row); index (the token narrowing row)
findings.defect: A later not narrowed entry is a widening of the blast radius back to every repository the account reaches. The rule's only answer is to restore two rows' text and review four rows. Nobody has to decide: no item goes to the operator, no deadline is set to re-narrow, and no compensating control is named for the interval beyond the security log, which records no merge or push.
findings.scenario: At the O6 sitting, read 1 finds the classic token again. The maintainer writes a not narrowed entry, restores the rows' text, and continues with block B. Nothing says when the narrowing returns, and the rows reviewed again stay as they were, since the rule asks only for a review.
findings.change: In the note: a not narrowed entry after a narrowed one is an item for the operator at that sitting, with two options, re-narrow before the sitting ends, or accept the widening with a date and the event that ends it; the entry records the answer. Cost: one sentence. No accepted risk of 05 5.4 changes: the token row's risk is the one already accepted, and this decides only how a lapse back into it is handled.
findings.evidence: Read at 54f674c: docs/notes/maintainer-block-of-ci-bootstrap.md:135-141 'A later entry whose verdict is not narrowed returns the token narrowing row of the index and the token row of [05 5.4] to the state before the narrowing, and is an event of those four rows too, so the decision each took on the narrowed premise is reviewed again'; docs/spec/05-security.md:392 (the token row) 'the GitHub security log is read at each sitting, as a judgment and not as a detector ... no pull request merge, push, tag creation, branch deletion or release change'.

findings.section: the note on the maintainer block (The token narrowing, the entry rule); 05 5.4 (the token row); index (the token narrowing row)
findings.defect: The return rule restores two rows 'to the state before the narrowing', but no rule makes the first narrowed entry edit them to an after-state: the 05 5.4 token row still says the narrowing 'is applied at the next maintainer sitting', and the index row already holds both states. A narrowed entry after a not narrowed one (re-narrowing) is no event at all, since only the first narrowed entry is one.
findings.scenario: The first entry says narrowed and nobody edits the 05 5.4 token row, which keeps saying the operator's token stands. Later a not narrowed entry 'returns' text that never changed, and a re-narrowed entry after it restores and fires nothing, so the four rows' review on the narrowed premise never happens again.
findings.change: In the note: the first narrowed entry edits the token row of 05 5.4 and the token narrowing row of the index to say the narrowing holds, with the entry's date, and any narrowed entry after a not narrowed one does the same and is an event of the four rows. Cost: two clauses. The token row's accepted risk is unchanged; only its statement of the current state is edited, as ADR 0011's consequences already ask ('say what was decided and what is pending').
findings.evidence: Read at 54f674c: docs/notes/maintainer-block-of-ci-bootstrap.md:132-134 'The first entry whose verdict is narrowed is the event of the four [Deferred decisions] rows'; docs/spec/05-security.md:392 'Narrowing the token was decided on 2026-10-09 ... and is applied at the next maintainer sitting, and the token stands until then'; docs/spec.md:348 'until the narrowing, the operator's own token and key ...; after it, the narrowed token'.

findings.section: the note on the maintainer block (Two limits of the entry); plan (block O8, Recommendation)
findings.defect: R16-11 was applied as M with a stated limit, but the limit lives only in the round record. The note's limits paragraph still names two limits, and O8's Recommendation recommends the dedicated socket without saying that the means is the maintainer's choice or what reopens it.
findings.scenario: A later reviewer of the token narrowing row reads the note's two limits and O8, finds a recommendation and no limit, and cannot tell that forwarding the host's own agent was accepted as allowed, nor that an authentication key found by read 2 is the reopener.
findings.change: Make the note's paragraph 'Three limits' and add: how the forwarding stops is the maintainer's choice (ADR 0011, decision 2, decides that it stops, not how); an entry whose read 2 finds an authentication key, or a second key (L2-r17-2), reopens it. Cost: one sentence.
findings.evidence: Read at 54f674c: docs/notes/maintainer-block-of-ci-bootstrap.md:184 'Two limits of the entry, stated and not closed (round 15)'; docs/plan.md:221 (O8 Recommendation) 'To stop the forwarding, forward a socket that holds only the signing key ... rather than the host's own agent; read 2 of the entry shows whether it holds'; docs/reviews/round-16.md (Write pass, R16-11) 'Stated limit: how the forwarding stops is the maintainer's choice'.

findings.defect: R16-09's edit, 'which the sandbox holds until block O8', ties the end of the operator's token to the block rather than to the first narrowed entry, and, in the sentence that explains why the maintainer pushes the `v*` tags, reads as if the tag ruleset binds the sandbox after O8. Whether the tag ruleset's bypass applies to the narrowed token is not predicted, and it stays not measured when `release.yml` lands first.
findings.scenario: O8 runs, read 1 differs and the entry says not narrowed; the plan still says the sandbox no longer holds the operator's token. Or a reader takes 'until block O8' to mean an agent may push the `v1.0.0` tag after O8, while the narrowed token, Contents write and the administrator's bypass, may still create it (inferred).
findings.change: Read 'which the sandbox holds until the note's first narrowed entry; whether the tag ruleset binds the narrowed token is measured only by an entry made before `release.yml` lands'. Cost: one clause.
findings.evidence: Read at 54f674c: docs/plan.md:202-204 'So are the two `v*` tags, which the maintainer pushes by working agreement, since the tag ruleset does not bind the operator's token, which the sandbox holds until block O8'; docs/notes/maintainer-block-of-ci-bootstrap.md (read 3 table, tag row) 'not predicted: whether the tag ruleset's bypass for the administrator role applies to a fine-grained token is not measured'; docs/spec.md:348 'whether it can create a `v*` tag through the tag ruleset's bypass is measured only by an entry made before `release.yml` lands'.

findings.section: plan (block O8); the note on the maintainer block (read 3, the merge try); ADR 0011 (decision 1)
findings.defect: O8 now holds decision 1 (remove the administrator bypass) and the entry, with no order between them, and read 3's merge try is expected 'accepted once its required checks are green', so it can show neither whether the narrowed token rides the bypass nor that decision 1 holds. Decision 1's only evidence is an API answer, not a try.
findings.scenario: The maintainer writes the entry first and removes the bypass afterwards. The merge try waits for green and is accepted, as expected; whether a fine-grained token of the administrator merges without the checks while the bypass stands is never seen, and decision 1 is never tried live.
findings.change: In O8: decision 1 first, then the entry. In read 3, the merge try is made once before the required checks are green, expected refused, then after they are green, expected accepted. Cost: one clause in O8 and one row note in the table. ADR 0011 decision 1 is unchanged; its evidence stays the API answer, and the try adds a reading.
findings.evidence: Read at 54f674c: docs/plan.md:221 (O8) 'write the dated entry of the note on the maintainer block and run the required-name try; and decision 1 of the same record, item a of the maintainer block: remove the administrator role from the bypass list'; docs/notes/maintainer-block-of-ci-bootstrap.md (read 3 table) 'accepted once its required checks are green, since the token keeps Contents and Pull requests write; this answer does not tell the two tokens apart'.

what_is_missing: Reads due at the events that change the narrowed state (sandbox re-creation or restart, a secret set again, token replacement with item h re-run, after the host pushes in a sitting) and after O7; what becomes of a global github secret; 'exactly one key' in read 2, as 06 6.4 says; an operator decision with a deadline when an entry reverses the narrowing; the forward edit of the two token rows at the first narrowed entry and a rule for re-narrowing; the R16-11 limit in the note; an order inside O8 and a merge try that can tell a bypass apart; 'until the first narrowed entry' in the plan's opening.
postmortem: After v1.0.0 the development sandbox is re-created, as a disposable sandbox is, and takes the global github secret, the operator's broad token (inferred). No read is due after O7, so the note's last entry still says narrowed, the 05 5.4 token row was never edited either way, and the four rows fired on the narrowed premise stay fired. Issue text steers an agent that now reaches every repository of the account; the security log records no merge or push, so nothing is seen. Even with the narrowed token, a second key in the forwarded socket can write elsewhere over SSH. What this person would not say aloud: every proof is a review reading in sittings already full (O6 is about 90 minutes per host), so the later reads are the first thing dropped; the stated limit of R16-11 lives only in a review record; and the rule for a lapse rewrites text instead of asking anyone to decide. It crosses the note (cadence, read 2, return rule, limits), 10 10.2 items g and h, the plan's opening and O8, the index token rows, the 05 5.4 token row and 06 6.4.
lens_critique: The lens counts success as the one widening decision written down with its control and its trigger. For this product the narrowing is a state that must stay true across disposable sandboxes and replaced credentials, and a control that is a human reading at fixed sittings is calendar-driven where the threat is event-driven. The lens should ask what events can silently undo a recorded mitigation, and whether its lapse forces a decision, not only whether its adoption was recorded.
missing_viewpoint: A credential and identity lifecycle owner: someone who tracks where each secret is stored (global versus per sandbox), when it expires or is regenerated, and what a re-created environment inherits. None of L0 to L16 owns that lifecycle; L2 sees the boundary, L7 the release chain, L15 moving ground, but none the life of a token.
out_of_scope: Lens bullet reconcile: (1) agent output as data, I24, I29, boundary A: out of this round's scope. (2) symlinks and '..' in a memory directory, os.Root: out of this round's scope. (3) the sandbox holding the operator's account with administrator rights, ADR 0008, control a human reading the security log (05 5.4): confirmed and extended, in scope; the narrowing that bounds it can lapse unseen (L2-r17-1, L2-r17-3), and the security log stays a judgment that records no merge or push (05 5.4, the token row). (4) side channels in the ledger, I33: out of this round's scope. (5) boundary B, secret names in the spec and values on the host: partly in scope and confirmed in shape, since a global versus sandbox-scoped github secret is exactly a value-on-host question the plan does not settle (L2-r17-1); the error-path leak is out of scope. (6) romeu acting on the wrong sandbox, boundary F, I26: out of this round's scope. Also out of scope: the salvage text of the delta (04, 01 1.6, 03 3.8, 08 8.5, I17, T068), and item h's workflow token (GITHUB_TOKEN versus the narrowed token), which predates the delta.
confidence: High on L2-r17-3, -4, -5, -6 and -7 (read from the text). Medium on L2-r17-2 (the mismatch with 06 6.4 is read; where GitHub lists deploy keys is inferred). Medium-low on the sandbox re-creation path of L2-r17-1 (secret precedence, sbx forwarding the caller's SSH_AUTH_SOCK and AddKeysToAgent re-adding a key are inferred; the host and sbx were not read), high on its cadence part (no read after O7 is read from the text).
